exposure: Absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) in the umbilical artery
cohort: Eighty-five pregnant women diagnosed with absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) in the umbilical artery Doppler were included.
finding: Absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) in the umbilical artery is a significant predictor of adverse perinatal outcomes, including high perinatal mortality and severe neonatal complications.
mod_finding: A high cesarean delivery rate (89.4%) was observed in pregnancies complicated by AEDF, primarily due to fetal distress.
